note: Phrase Ladder sentences (22 Nov 2026). Same marks as the Phrase Bank: {…} is the expression, […] its key word. belt: the cards View shows for a job, one expression each, all on ONE topic so they read as one essay; the first is the phrase to learn and must match the ladder's lead phrase. practice: the lead phrase in three sentences on three topics (smartphones, online learning, tourism), used by the practice steps in turn. Tasks without an entry fall back to the bare phrases.

belt: {Few people would [deny] that} smartphones have changed the way teenagers learn.
{It is widely [recognised] that} smartphones have changed the way teenagers learn.
{It is often [argued] that} smartphones have changed the way teenagers learn.
{There is no [doubt] that} smartphones have become part of every school day.
{[Nowadays],} smartphones are part of almost every teenager's school day.
practice: {Few people would deny that} smartphones have changed the way teenagers learn.
{Few people would deny that} online courses have become part of everyday life.
{Few people would deny that} tourism has changed many small towns.

belt: {In this essay I will [explain] why I believe that} phones belong in the classroom.
{This essay will [argue] that} phones can make lessons more effective.
{I intend to [show] that} phones do far more good than harm at school.
{I will set out the [reasons] why} I support phones in class.
{This essay will make clear [where] I stand on} phones in the classroom.
practice: {In this essay I will explain why I believe that} phones belong in the classroom.
{In this essay I will explain why I believe that} they are good for students.
{In this essay I will explain why I believe that} it does more harm than good.

belt: {[Firstly],} phones give students instant access to information.
{To [begin] with,} phones give students instant access to information.
{First of [all],} phones give students instant access to information.
{In the first [place],} phones give students instant access to information.
{For one [thing],} phones give students instant access to information.
practice: {Firstly,} phones give students instant access to information.
{Firstly,} students can learn at their own pace.
{Firstly,} crowds make daily life difficult for residents.

belt: {One [reason] why I believe this is that} pupils can check facts in seconds.
{The [main] reason I hold this view is that} pupils can check facts in seconds.
{My [first] reason for thinking so is that} pupils can check facts in seconds.
{What matters [most] to me is that} pupils can check facts in seconds.
{The most [important] point is that} pupils can check facts in seconds.
practice: {One reason why I believe this is that} pupils can check facts in seconds.
{One reason why I believe this is that} nobody has to travel to school.
{One reason why I believe this is that} rents go up when flats become holiday homes.

belt: {[Moreover],} many apps make revision more enjoyable.
{[Furthermore],} many apps make revision more enjoyable.
{In [addition],} many apps make revision more enjoyable.
{What is [more],} many apps make revision more enjoyable.
{Apart from [that],} many apps make revision more enjoyable.
practice: {Moreover,} many apps make revision more enjoyable.
{Moreover,} recorded classes can be watched again before an exam.
{Moreover,} local shops are replaced by souvenir stalls.

belt: {A [further] reason is that} parents can contact their children easily.
{[Another] point that supports my view is that} parents can contact their children easily.
{An additional [consideration] is that} parents can contact their children easily.
{Equally [important] is the fact that} parents can contact their children easily.
{My second main [reason] is that} parents can contact their children easily.
practice: {A further reason is that} parents can contact their children easily.
{A further reason is that} online courses are often cheaper.
{A further reason is that} traffic and noise increase every summer.

belt: {Another [key] point is that} pupils need to learn to use technology responsibly.
{Last but not [least],} pupils need to learn to use technology responsibly.
{[Finally],} pupils need to learn to use technology responsibly.
{It is also [worth] mentioning that} pupils need to learn to use technology responsibly.
{On top of [this],} pupils need to learn to use technology responsibly.
practice: {Another key point is that} pupils need to learn to use technology responsibly.
{Another key point is that} students in small villages get the same chances.
{Another key point is that} historic buildings are damaged by so many visitors.

belt: {[Admittedly],} phones can be a distraction, {but} clear rules solve this.
{It is [true] that} phones can be a distraction, {but} clear rules solve this.
{[Although]} phones can be a distraction, clear rules solve this.
{Some people [argue] that} phones are a distraction. {However,} clear rules solve this.
{[Despite]} the risk of distraction, phones are worth having in class.
practice: {Admittedly,} phones can be a distraction, {but} clear rules solve this.
{Admittedly,} some learners miss their friends, {but} they can still meet at weekends.
{Admittedly,} tourism creates jobs, {but} most of them are badly paid.

belt: {All things [considered],} phones are a useful tool if they are used wisely.
{To sum [up],} phones are a useful tool if they are used wisely.
{All in [all],} phones are a useful tool if they are used wisely.
{On [balance],} phones are a useful tool if they are used wisely.
{In [conclusion],} phones are a useful tool if they are used wisely.
practice: {All things considered,} phones are a useful tool if they are used wisely.
{All things considered,} online learning gives students more freedom.
{All things considered,} mass tourism causes more problems than it solves.

belt: {I firmly [believe] that} schools should teach pupils to use them sensibly.
{In my [view],} schools should teach pupils to use them sensibly.
{It seems [clear] to me that} schools should teach pupils to use them sensibly.
{I am [convinced] that} schools should teach pupils to use them sensibly.
{For these [reasons], I believe that} schools should teach pupils to use them sensibly.
practice: {I firmly believe that} schools should teach pupils to use them sensibly.
{I firmly believe that} every school should offer it.
{I firmly believe that} councils should limit the number of visitors.
